stem: A client with a clinical condition associated with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) has a fibrinogen result within the laboratory reference interval. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: The normal fibrinogen value excludes DIC, so the remaining coagulation findings do not need to be considered in this clinical setting.
options.B: DIC requires a low fibrinogen value before the diagnosis can be considered, even when platelet, PT, or fibrin-marker abnormalities are present.
options.C: A normal fibrinogen value does not exclude DIC; interpretation requires the clinical setting plus the overall coagulation pattern, including platelets, PT/aPTT, fibrin markers, and fibrinogen.
options.D: Fibrinogen does not contribute to DIC evaluation, so its value should be omitted when the coagulation pattern and clinical setting are assessed.

rationale: Current StatPearls/NCBI guidance states that no single history, examination, or laboratory component can diagnose or rule out DIC. Evaluation uses the clinical context together with a pattern of findings that includes PT, aPTT, fibrinogen, platelet count, schistocytes, and fibrin-related markers. A decreased fibrinogen can support DIC, but a value within the reference interval cannot by itself exclude the disorder. C is therefore correct. A and B give fibrinogen inappropriate stand-alone exclusionary power, and D incorrectly removes a recognized component of DIC evaluation.
educational_objective: Avoid excluding DIC on the basis of one normal fibrinogen result; interpret fibrinogen as one component of the clinical and laboratory pattern used to evaluate suspected DIC.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf) / StatPearls
source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; article last updated May 1, 2024; live NCBI page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Evaluation: no single history, physical examination, or laboratory component can diagnose or rule out DIC; suggestive pattern includes increased PT/aPTT, decreased fibrinogen, reduced platelet count/hematocrit, schistocytes and fibrin split products; scoring incorporates platelets, fibrin markers, PT and fibrinogen.
source_claim_supported: No single laboratory component, including fibrinogen, can rule out DIC; evaluation requires the clinical setting and the overall coagulation pattern.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — review laboratory results and recognize complications/risk patterns.
correction_summary: Removed distractor-only 'only' wording and balanced option lengths while preserving the required multi-parameter interpretation of suspected DIC.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — NCBI explicitly states that no single laboratory component can diagnose or rule out DIC; C is uniquely consistent with the cited evaluation framework.
